lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be left off the résumé.
items.because: They are not evidence of qualifications and can introduce irrelevant screening considerations.

items.says: The same triage-branch achievement appears twice with inconsistent reduction figures.
items.because: One entry says 68% and the other says two-thirds, making the résumé look padded and weakening trust.

items.says: EXPERIENCE should appear above EDUCATION, with EDUCATION after PROJECTS.
items.because: The software-to-ML progression is stronger evidence of capability than the current M.S.

items.says: The résumé has an unexplained 10-month gap from Jun 2022 to May 2023.
items.because: The unexplained interval can create uncertainty about the timeline.

items.says: The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement lacks a baseline and does not say whether it is relative or percentage points.
items.because: A reader cannot precisely judge the result or compare it with the starting performance.

items.says: The routing bullet incorrectly uses the plural possessive “their” with “each.”
items.because: Each specialist agent individually takes the singular possessive “its.”

items.says: The indirect phrase “limits each ... to their in-scope signals” makes the routing action hard to scan.
items.because: The reader must parse the restriction before seeing what the router does.

items.says: The phrase “cutting tool calls per case 18%” is grammatically incomplete without “by.”
items.because: The missing preposition makes the amount of reduction unclear and looks unpolished.

items.says: The long method chain buries the performance results and baseline comparison.
items.because: GRPO, grouped rollouts, and reward design appear before the evidence of fewer calls, lower latency, and equal accuracy.

items.says: The harness bullet does not state how catching two regressions benefited the release or users.
items.because: The practical consequence of finding the regressions is unclear.

items.says: The phrase “the team used to compare” weakens ownership of the harness.
items.because: The indirect clause shifts attention from the delivered capability to the team.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking is overstated as making the model reproduce tool outputs more faithfully.
items.because: The method changes which tokens contribute to loss but does not itself supervise or guarantee faithful tool-output reproduction.

items.says: The bullet describes an intended effect rather than a measured result and does not identify the assessed tool outputs.
items.because: “Would learn” states a goal, while “the tool outputs” provides no output type or evaluation basis.

items.says: The dense modifier “with ML-extracted features” and the compound “pending-case backlog” slow the operational result.
items.because: Their meaning is harder to scan than a direct description of the screening action and backlog.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking work is duplicated across two bullets.
items.because: The earlier bullet already gives the accuracy result, so repetition consumes a bullet without adding a separate achievement.

items.says: Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision does not by itself support a 4x reduction in total fine-tuning GPU memory.
items.because: BF16 can roughly halve eligible tensors while FP32 optimizer states, gradients, master weights, and other overhead remain.

items.says: The 4x memory reduction lacks a baseline and does not state what the reduction enabled.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what was measured or judge the result's practical value.

items.says: The load-test clause uses present-tense “fail” inside an otherwise past-tense bullet.
items.because: The role ended in Jul 2024, so the tense makes the safeguard's timing unclear.

items.says: The bullet incorrectly mixes past-tense “Maintained” with present-tense “adds.”
items.because: The ended role requires a consistent past time frame.

items.says: The release-cycle result gives the ending duration of three days but not the starting duration.
items.because: Without the comparison, a reader cannot judge the scale of the improvement.

items.says: “Maintained the CI pipeline” frames the work as a duty instead of leading with the result-producing action.
items.because: The automated regression checks and release-cycle result are stronger evidence of engineering impact.

items.says: The claim that nightly backlogs were removed is not quantified.
items.because: The 30-service count shows contribution scale but not how much the dispatch problem improved.

items.says: “Accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams” gives generic benefits without identifying what changed.
items.because: The impact remains a general assertion rather than an observable result.

items.says: The delivery and downstream-team claims lack a figure or comparison.
items.because: Without a baseline, delta, adoption count, or other anchor, their size and credibility cannot be judged.

items.says: “Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices” does not identify the practices or the work used to drive adoption.
items.because: The phrase could describe tooling, workflow changes, training, or other activities, making ownership difficult to evaluate.

items.says: “Working context” and “the raw conversation grew 100x” are undefined.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what resource was bounded or what baseline the 100x comparison used.

items.says: The concurrency and cache controls are not sufficient on their own to claim that deadlocks and lost tool results were removed.
items.because: Separate pools can still deadlock, and completion-gated writes do not guarantee durability through cancellation, retries, or failure.

items.says: “Under 50-way fan-out” gives test scale but not the measured change in deadlocks or lost tool results.
items.because: The reader cannot tell how often the system failed before or what evidence shows the fix worked.

items.says: “Under 50-way fan-out” does not clearly identify a test condition, capacity limit, or supported operating point.
items.because: The ambiguity weakens the technical description of the concurrency result.

items.says: The eight-metric integration does not state what changed because of the work.
items.because: The bullet reports implementation volume without showing its effect on coverage, consistency, comparisons, or manual work.

items.says: The bullet does not explain how the metric integration was implemented.
items.because: Without an implementation detail, the contribution reads as a count rather than evidence of technical ownership.

items.says: “Showed the evaluator tracks” is missing “that,” and “showed” does not specify the validation action.
items.because: The missing word is ungrammatical, while the vague verb leaves the candidate's action unclear.

items.says: A Kendall correlation of 0.89 does not by itself establish that the evaluator broadly “tracks” degradation.
items.because: It supports rank association but does not establish sensitivity, validity, calibration, or causal response.

items.says: The Kendall correlation does not say what it was measured against.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it compares evaluator scores with degradation severity, a ranking, or another reference.

items.says: The evaluation-framework project contains an unrelated triage achievement duplicated from the Mobility Systems Company entry.
items.because: The copied sensor-triage result breaks the project's coherent focus on research-agent evaluation.
